Rashi on Chullin 72a:10:2.hebrew: מת - דבר שמיתה באה על ידו, דהיינו רביעית:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:10:2.english: Corpse [met] - something through which death comes [when lost], that is, a quarter-[log of blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:11:1.english: The flesh is [ritually] pure - because an animal does not contract ritual impurity while alive:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:11:2.hebrew: הבשר מגע נבלה - בשר העובר, מגע אבר מן החי שהוא מטמא כנבלה, בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכט:). אי נמי, אם יצא עובר מת, נבלה גמורה הוי האבר, מאחר שלא טהרתו שחיטת אמו:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:11:2.english: The flesh [is impure due to] contact with a carcass - [That is,] the flesh of the fetus [is impure through] contact with a limb from a living animal, which imparts impurity like a carcass, [as taught] in [the chapter] Ha'Or VeHaRotev (below, Chullin 129b). Alternatively, if the fetus emerged dead, the limb is a full carcass, since its mother's slaughter did not purify it:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:12:1.hebrew: מגע טרפה שחוטה - שהשחיטה, אע"פ שאינה מתרת האבר באכילה, מטהרתו מידי נבלה, והויא כטרפה שחוטה שאינה מטמאה מן התורה — כדמפרש ואזיל — אלא מדרבנן במוקדשין:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:12:1.english: Contact with a tereifa that was slaughtered - For the slaughter, even though it does not permit the limb to be eaten, purifies it from [the status of] neveilah, so that it is like a slaughtered tereifa, which does not impart ritual impurity by Torah law — as [the Gemara] goes on to explain — but rather [only] by rabbinic decree with respect to consecrated [foods].

Rashi on Chullin 72a:1:1.hebrew: והא עובר וחיה - דקתני מתני': החיה טמאה שבעה, והאשה טהורה:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:1:1.english: And [what about] a fetus and a midwife - as the Mishnah teaches: The midwife is impure [for] seven [days], and the woman is pure:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:1:2.hebrew: וקמטמי לה עובר לחיה - ש"מ דטעמא דאשה טהורה משום מגע בית הסתרים הוא, ולא משום בלוע:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:1:2.english: And the fetus renders the midwife impure - Conclude from this that the reason the woman is pure is because [it is] contact in a concealed place, and not because [it is] swallowed:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:2:1.english: A ring will not ultimately leave - [This is asked] in astonishment:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:3:2.hebrew: מאי אינה מדברי תורה - ל"ל למימר כולי האי? לימא "טומאה זו דברי סופרים" משום גזירה, כדמפרש לקמיה:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:3:2.english: What [is the meaning of] "it is not by Torah law" - Why did he need to say all this? Let him [simply] say "this impurity is [by] rabbinic law" because of a decree, as [the Gemara] explains further on:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:3:3.hebrew: לא תימא - מתני' ר"ע היא, דאמר: עובר מת שבמעי אשה טמא; הלכך מטמא לחיה, דטומאה בלועה מטמאה וטהרה בלועה מיטמא, ואשה טהורה משום דמגע בית הסתרים הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:3:3.english: Do not say - [that] the Mishnah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Akiva, who says: A dead fetus in a woman's womb is impure; therefore, it imparts impurity to the midwife, for swallowed impurity imparts impurity and swallowed purity contracts impurity, and the woman [herself] is pure because it is contact in a concealed place:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:3:4.hebrew: אלא אפי' לר' ישמעאל כו' - ולקמן בעי מאי ר' ישמעאל ור"ע:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:3:4.english: Rather, even [according to] Rabbi Yishmael, etc. - And later [the Gemara] asks: What is [the teaching of] Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva?

Rashi on Chullin 72a:4:1.hebrew: גזירה שמא יוציא כו' - דאי אמרת חיה שפשטה ידה למעי אשה ונגעה בעובר מת טהורה, פעמים שהולד מוציא ראשו חוץ לפרוזדור והרי הוא כילוד ומטמא, וכסבורה חיה שעדיין הוא במעיה ואתי לטהרה. אבל ברועה שהושיט ידו למעי בהמה, דקתני מתני' טהור, ליכא למיגזר הכי, מפני שרחם שלה גלוי, דכי מפיק חזי ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:4:1.english: A decree lest [the fetus] extend [its head], etc. - For if you say [that] a midwife who stretched her hand into a woman's womb and touched a dead fetus is ritually pure, sometimes the fetus extends its head outside the prozdor [birth canal], and it is [then] considered as born and imparts ritual impurity, while the midwife thinks that it is still inside her womb, and [people] would come to declare her ritually pure. However, regarding a shepherd who stretched his hand into an animal's womb — where the Mishnah teaches [that he is] ritually pure — there is no [reason] to make such a decree, because its womb is exposed, so that when [the fetus] extends [its head], he sees it:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:5:1.hebrew: טרידא - עסוקה היא בחבליה וציריה, וטרידא מלומר לחיה "אל תגעי":
Rashi on Chullin 72a:5:1.english: [She is] distracted - She is preoccupied with her labor pains and pangs, and is [too] distracted to say to the midwife, "Do not touch."

Rashi on Chullin 72a:6:1.english: On the face of the field - implies [something] exposed:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:6:2.english: To exclude a fetus - because it is concealed [in the womb]:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:6:3.english: Golel - The cover of a corpse's coffin:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:1.english: Dofek [grave wall] - A board that they place at its [the grave's] side:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:2.hebrew: ור' ישמעאל סבר גולל ודופק הלכתא היא - וכי אתא קרא, להוציא עובר:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:2.english: And Rabbi Yishmael holds [that] the grave cover and grave walls are [a traditional] law - and when the verse comes, [it comes] to exclude a fetus:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:3.hebrew: ור"ע סבר עובר במעי אשה טמא - וכי אתא קרא לגולל ודופק, וקסבר לאו הלכתא היא:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:3.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds [that] a fetus in a woman's womb is impure - and when the verse comes, [it comes] for the grave cover and the grave walls, and he holds [that their impurity] is not a [Sinaitic] tradition:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:4.hebrew: מדאורייתא מנא ליה - דטמא, דלא מטהר ליה ממשמעותיה ד"על פני השדה", ואפי' לא מייתר:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:4.english: By Torah law, from where does he [derive it] - [namely,] that it is impure, such that he does not declare it pure from the plain meaning of "on the open field" (Numbers 19:16), even if [that phrase] is not superfluous:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:7:5.english: Of a corpse, of the life - A corpse that is inside another person:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:8:1.hebrew: רביעית הלוג דם, חיי האדם תלויין בו, שבכך הוא מתקיים:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:8:1.english: A quarter-log of blood — a person's life depends on it, for with that [amount] he survives:

Rashi on Chullin 72a:9:1.hebrew: אף רביעית דם הבא משני מתים - הלכך, האי קרא דכתיב ביה חד נפש, לאו לרביעית דם אתא:
Rashi on Chullin 72a:9:1.english: Even a quarter-[log] of blood that comes from two corpses - Therefore, this verse in which a single soul is written does not come [to teach] regarding a quarter-[log] of blood:

Tosafot on Chullin 72a:10:1.hebrew: שתי נפשות ושיעור אחד - ור' ישמעאל סבר דיש אם למסורת, ו"נפשת" כתיב, כדאמר בסנהדרין בפ"ק (דף ד.). וקשה, דתרי קראי ברביעית דם ל"ל: "במת בנפש" ו"נפש":
Tosafot on Chullin 72a:10:1.english: Two people and one measure - And Rabbi Yishmael holds that the traditional written text is authoritative, and nafshat [i.e., nafshot written defectively, in the singular] is written, as [the Gemara] says in Sanhedrin in the first chapter (4a). And it is difficult: why do we need two verses regarding a quarter-[log] of blood — "[whoever touches] a corpse, the soul [bemet benefesh]" [Numbers 19:13], and "soul [nefesh]" [in Leviticus 21:11]:

Tosafot on Chullin 72a:11:1.hebrew: הוציא עובר את ידו וחתכה ואח"כ שחט את אמו הבשר טהור - דעובר שבפנים, אפי' מת, חשיב כחי, דהא קא מהני ליה שחיטת אמו להתירו אף באכילה:
Tosafot on Chullin 72a:11:1.english: The fetus extended its foreleg and [one] severed it and afterward slaughtered its mother, the flesh is pure - For a fetus inside [the womb], even if it died, is considered as alive, since its mother's slaughter is effective for it to permit it even for eating:

Tosafot on Chullin 72a:12:1.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים מגע טרפה שחוטה - בשחיטה עושה ניפול פליגי, כדאמר בגמ'. וקודם שחיטה לכ"ע אדם שנוגע באבר שבחוץ טהור, דאי מחיים מטמא, היכי הוה מהני שחיטה לרבנן להפקיע הטומאה לטהרות? ולעיל דקתני "הושיט רועה את ידו ונגע בו — טהור", לאו דוקא לפי שהוא בפנים, דאפי' הוציא עובר ידו לחוץ ונגע בו הרועה טהור; אלא להודיעך כחו דר' יוסי הגלילי, דאפי' הכי בטמאה טמא. א"נ מודו רבנן בהוציא ידו לחוץ ונגע בו דבטמאה טמא, דלענין מה שבפנים הוא דמקשינן טמאה לטהורה, ולא לענין מה שבחוץ:
Tosafot on Chullin 72a:12:1.english: And the Rabbis say: Contact with a tereifa that was slaughtered - They disagree regarding [whether] slaughter causes [the protruding limb to be considered] fallen [off], as stated in the Gemara. And prior to slaughter, according to all opinions, a person who touches the limb that is outside [the womb] is ritually pure; for if it imparted ritual impurity while [the mother was] alive, how would slaughter avail according to the Rabbis to remove the ritual impurity with respect to ritually pure foods? And [as for] what was taught above: "If the shepherd extended his hand [into the womb] and touched it, he is ritually pure," [this is] not specifically because it is inside [the womb], for even if the fetus extended its foreleg outside and the shepherd touched it, he is ritually pure; rather, [it was stated that way] to inform you of the extent of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili's [opinion], that even so, in [the case of] a non-kosher [animal], he is ritually impure. Alternatively, the Rabbis concede regarding [a case where the fetus] extended its foreleg outside and he touched it, that in [the case of] a non-kosher [animal] he is ritually impure, for it is [only] with respect to what is inside [the womb] that we compare a non-kosher [animal] to a kosher [animal], and not with respect to what is outside:

Tosafot on Chullin 72a:1:1.hebrew: והרי חיה ועובר דכשתי טבעות דמו - מה שפי' בקונטרס, אלמא דטומאה בלועה מטמאה, וטעמא דאשה טהורה משום בית הסתרים, וכן פי' בסמוך גבי "לא תימא מתני' ר' עקיבא היא" — וקשה: נהי דמגע בית הסתרים לא מטמא, במשא מטמא! אלא צ"ל כדפירשנו, דאשה טהורה משום טומאה בלועה היא, וחיה הויא כשתי טבעות:
Tosafot on Chullin 72a:1:1.english: Now behold, the midwife and the fetus are like two rings - [As for] that which Rashi explained — [namely,] that [this] implies that swallowed impurity imparts impurity, and the reason the woman is pure is because of [contact in a] concealed area, and he likewise explained [so] nearby regarding "Do not say the Mishnah is [the view of] R. Akiva" — [this is] difficult: granted that contact in a concealed area does not impart impurity, through carrying it [still] imparts impurity! Rather, one must say as we explained [earlier], that the woman is pure because it is swallowed impurity, and [the case of] the midwife is [what is] like two rings:

Tosafot on Chullin 72a:4:1.hebrew: גזירה שמא יוציא ולד ראשו וכו' - פי' בקונטרס משום דהרי הוא כילוד, משמע דדוקא נקט ראשו. וכן משמע בפ' יוצא דופן (נדה דף מב:) גבי "יולדת מטמאה בפנים כבחוץ", דקאמר: כגון שהוציא ולד ראשו חוץ לפרוזדור, כדר' אושעיא כו'; משמע דר' אושעיא נקט דוקא ראשו. ותימה: דאמאי נקט ראשו? אפי' הוציא ידו חוץ לפרוזדור נמי נטמאה החיה שנגעה בו או הסיטה, דתו לאו טומאה בלועה היא! וי"ל דגזירת הכתוב היא, דעד שיהא כילוד לא מטמאה, כדדריש מ"על פני השדה". והשתא ניחא הא דצריך ר' ישמעאל למדרש טעמא מקרא, דטעמיה פשוט דטומאה בלועה היא, אלא משום דלא מטמא בהוציא ידו עד שיהא כילוד. ור' עקיבא נמי לא פליג אלא בהוציא את ידו. וכן משמע "דלא תימא אליבא דר"ע", משמע דכר"ע אתיא מתני' בפשיטות, דטמאה החיה מדברי סופרים, דגזרינן כולו במעי אשה אטו הוציא ידו; אבל אי ר"ע מטמא עובר במעי אמו אפי' לא יצא לחוץ כלל, היכי מתוקמא מתניתא אליביה, דחיה טמאה ואשה טהורה:
Tosafot on Chullin 72a:4:1.english: A decree lest the fetus extend its head, etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Because it is like one born. This implies that he specifically stated "its head." And so it is implied in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 42b) regarding [the Mishnah,] "A woman in childbirth conveys impurity inside as outside," where [the Gemara] says: "For example, where the fetus extended its head outside the prozdor [birth canal], in accordance with [the statement of] R. Oshaya, etc." — this implies that R. Oshaya specifically stated "its head." And this is astonishing: why did he state "its head"? Even if it extended its hand outside the prozdor, the midwife who touched it or moved it should also become impure, since it is no longer a swallowed impurity! And one can answer that it is a scriptural decree that until it is like one born, it does not convey impurity, as [the Gemara] derives from "upon the open field" [Numbers 19:16]. And now it is understandable why R. Yishmael needs to derive his reason from a verse — for [otherwise] his reason is obvious, that it is a swallowed impurity — rather, [he needs the verse] because it does not convey impurity when it extends its hand, until it is like one born. And R. Akiva also only disagrees in [the case where] it extended its hand. And so it is implied from [the Gemara saying,] "so that you should not say [it is] according to R. Akiva" — this implies that according to R. Akiva, our Mishnah is understood straightforwardly, that the midwife is impure by rabbinic decree, because we decree [impurity when] it is entirely in the woman's womb on account of [the case where] it extended its hand; but if R. Akiva declares a fetus in its mother's womb impure [by Torah law] even if it did not emerge outside at all, how could the Mishnah be established according to him, [when it states] that the midwife is impure and the woman is pure:

Tosafot on Chullin 72a:6:1.hebrew: גולל ודופק - מפורש בפ"ק דכתובות (דף ד: ד"ה עד):
Tosafot on Chullin 72a:6:1.english: The grave cover and the grave walls - [This is] explained in the first chapter of Ketubot (4b, s.v. "Ad"):
